description: Keep timestamped log identifiers and return those in a requested inclusive time span at one of six granularities. Example 1: after recording two logs in January and one in February, a January-month query returns the first two IDs in time order. Example 2: a query restricted to one second returns only logs whose timestamp has that exact second. Constraints: timestamps use the fixed YYYY:MM:DD:HH:MM:SS layout, IDs are unique, and granularity is Year, Month, Day, Hour, Minute, or Second.
intuition: A fixed timestamp format makes prefix comparison sufficient to truncate the requested granularity.

brute_force.approach: Store every log and scan all records on each retrieval.
brute_force.time: put O(1), retrieve O(n log n) to return chronological IDs

optimal.approach: Keep records ordered by timestamp, compare the relevant timestamp prefixes, and emit matching IDs in order.

edge_cases: Both endpoints are inclusive at the selected granularity.
Several logs may share one timestamp.
